text:
client_dev: Hey support, we've got a steady trickle of users failing login via our mobile app. The provider (Google) returns code + state but when we redeem the code we get `invalid_grant` and server logs show `pkce_verifier_mismatch`. Happens only from mobile deep links (iOS universal links and Android app link). Desktop web flows are fine.

priya_support: Thanks — can you share an example redirect URL you see on the device and what the app hands to your backend? Also are you using the S256 PKCE method?

client_dev: Yes S256. Example (captured via device logs):
```
https://auth.myprod.com/callback?code=4/0AY0e-g...&state=st_9b2f...&code_challenge=Abc+XyZ/123==
```
But when the app posts /oauth/token it sends the code_verifier we generated earlier and server computes challenge and they don't match.

ryan_mobile: Quick head's up: Android's Intent/Uri decoding and some in-app browsers treat `+` as space unless the param is percent-encoded. If your code_challenge has `+` or `/` (i.e., regular base64) it can get converted to space which will obviously break PKCE. Same for `=` padding which some layers drop.

priya_support: Do you generate the code_challenge using base64 (standard) or base64url? Per RFC7636 you need base64url without padding.

client_dev: Uh oh, we used node's `Buffer.from(...).toString('base64')` then replaced `+`/`/` manually in some places but not consistently. Our code: 
```js
const verifier = randomString(64);
const challenge = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(verifier).digest('base64');
// later: encode for url
const qc = encodeURIComponent(challenge);
```
We thought encodeURIComponent would be enough.

ana_security: encodeURIComponent won't change `+` to `%2B` if the value had a `+` created by base64? Actually encodeURIComponent of `+` yields `%2B` so that should be ok if applied everywhere. But if some intermediate step uses `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` decoding semantics (e.g., Intent.getQueryParameter on Android) `+` becomes ' ' unless it was percent-encoded as `%2B`. If you double-encode inconsistently you get mismatches. Also some CDNs or trackers decode querystrings before forwarding.

ops_cdn: We looked at edge logs for the failing requests and saw the raw request path contained `+` and `/` characters in the querystrings. However some of our edge rules url-decode values for logging and then re-encode — if your app later reads from the decoded form that could change things. We did not actively replace `+` with space but if a client library decodes as form-encoded that will.

priya_support: Can you reproduce locally with an Android emulator using the app link? Try logging the exact intent data received by the app (android logs show the raw URI) and compare with what you send to the backend.

client_dev: Repro steps we used:
1) Generate verifier in app using current code
2) Open Chrome Custom Tab -> provider auth -> provider redirects to universal link -> app receives intent
3) App extracts `code_challenge` and `state` with `Uri.getQueryParameter()` then does POST to our /oauth/token with code_verifier
Observed that `Uri.getQueryParameter("code_challenge")` returns a string with spaces where `+` used to be.

ryan_mobile: That's the known behavior: `Uri.getQueryParameter()` treats `+` as space. Workarounds: ensure code_challenge uses base64url (so no `+` or `/` and no `=` padding), or percent-encode `+` as `%2B` before redirect. Simpler: compute code_challenge using base64url (replace `+`-> `-`, `/`-> `_`, remove `=` padding).

client_dev: We switched generator to: 
```js
function base64url(input) {
  return input.replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, '');
}
const challenge = base64url(crypto.createHash('sha256').update(verifier).digest('base64'));
```
Deployed this to our mobile build and server verification code also updated to compute base64url.

priya_support: Any other layers that might touch querystring? Apple Universal Links handoff to app should preserve percent-encoding, but some analytics SDKs (branch, adjust) rewrite URLs and may decode then re-encode. Did you instrument third-party SDKs?

client_dev: Good call. We had Branch SDK in the middle for attribution, it was rewriting the URL and not preserving percent-encoding for `+`. We disabled Branch for the auth path and the problem rate dropped.

ops_cdn: Also note CloudFront and some older load balancers may normalize URLs and drop trailing `=` padding for logging. Using base64url avoids `=` so it's more robust across CDNs.

ana_security: Security note: ensure you never accept `code_challenge` computed with standard base64; require S256 base64url only. Also rotate verifier length if you switch. Log mismatch cases with obfuscated values for postmortem.

client_dev: After switching to base64url and bypassing Branch on the auth flow we've seen near-zero `pkce_verifier_mismatch` in mobile. Thanks.

priya_support: TL;DR for the ticket: root cause was using standard base64 & relying on intermediate layers that treat `+` as space or drop padding. Fixes: 1) compute PKCE S256 challenge as base64url (no +/=), 2) avoid third-party URL rewrites in auth redirect path or ensure they preserve percent-encoding, 3) add backend validation to reject non-base64url challenges and log failures.

auth-bot: Escalation created: AUTH-3182 "Mobile deep link PKCE failures: use base64url and avoid URL-rewriting SDKs" assigned to ryan_mobile.

client_dev: We'll keep this thread open for 48h while monitoring — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
